title: Gradual model rollout failure debrief and synthetic safety suite
creator: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary:

During a staged canary rollout of v2.4.0-quantized on 2026-02-16 we observed a steady increase in user-visible semantic regressions (elevated hallucination and formatting errors) starting at 8% traffic. The automated rollback did not trigger because the rollout health check relied on an aggregated latency+error metric that did not capture output-quality drift. Shadow traffic tests had shown no signal because the shadow path used an expired KV-cache warmup and a different batching boundary, producing different model context behavior.

Root causes identified:
1) Canary health criteria omitted structured-output quality metrics (semantic-similarity scoring and hallucination rate) and used a threshold tuned for endpoint errors only.
2) Shadow traffic configuration used sampling with a truncated prefix and an empty KV warmup; the shadow run could not reproduce stateful cache behavior.
3) The model variant's tokenization/quantization path produced nondeterministic rounding at long prefix lengths; at 1.2k+ context length we saw divergence in beam/search fallback behavior.
4) The rollback automation had a hysteresis window of 30 minutes before action and required a concurrent latency spike; the regression was gradual and below those thresholds.

Actions taken (during incident):
- Immediate canary pause at 12:32 UTC and 100% rollback to previous model by Ops.
- Rapid scoreboard of customer-facing errors; CS notified and a proactive email sent to top-10 impacted accounts.
- PagerDuty post-incident paging and formation of an investigation pod (Ava, Liam, Priya, Mateo).

Deliverables from this ticket:
- Formalized synthetic safety-suite (see tests) to run as pre-rollout gating.
- Runbook updates for canary pause, expedited rollback, and emergency reconfiguration of traffic-weight hysteresis.
- Telemetry additions: per-candidate semantic-similarity metric, hallucination rate, and prefix-length stratification in dashboards.
- Automated rollback rule changes and a staged rollout slow-start policy.

Runbook excerpt (operational playbook to be added to Console -> Rollouts -> Runbooks):
1) Detection: If semantic-similarity(deployed, baseline) drops >= 6% over 3 contiguous 5-minute buckets for canary fraction >= 5%, mark health as degraded.
2) Isolation: Immediately clamp canary rollout to 0% traffic. Verify secondary routing fallback to last-stable model.
3) Cutover: If rollback succeeds, notify on-call, open a rollback-change PR and start root-cause investigation channel.
4) Escalation: If rollback fails or anomalies persist post-rollback, escalate to SRE lead and open incident Commander role.
5) Postmortem: Create incident retro within 72 hours with timeline, telemetry snapshots, and PR links.

Safety-suite (high level):
- Synthetic Traffic Harness: deterministic prompt corpus that exercises long-tail prefixes, multi-turn state, and structured outputs (tables, JSON).
- KV Warmup Simulator: replicate client prefix loading to ensure KV cache warming occurs for shadow and canary runs.
- Output-Quality Checks: automated semantic similarity (embedding cosine), hallucination heuristics, and structured-output schema validators.
- Divergence Detector: lightweight run-time that compares top-1/top-N token distributions between baseline and candidate on matched inputs.
- Canary Ramp Policy Tests: simulate incremental 1%->10%->50% ramps with synthetic traffic to validate thresholds and latency impacts.

Acceptance criteria for the safety-suite (for release gating):
- For 10k synthetic inputs representative of production, no regression in semantic-similarity beyond the calibrated delta and hallucination rate must be below 0.5% on the suite.
- Shadow path must reproduce at least 95% of KV cache accesses seen in production traces.
- Automated rollback rules trigger within 3 minutes of meeting quality degradation signals during synthetic run.

Notes on implementable mitigations (engineering):
- Add per-request trace ID propagation from console -> runtime -> model to correlate outputs with request topologies.
- Introduce prefix-length stratified metrics and cache hit/miss histograms per model variant.
- Tighten rollout hysteresis: allow quality-only triggers (no latency spike required) and expose a tunable sensitivity per-project.
- Deploy quantization A/B harness to validate numeric stability at long contexts.

Communication & follow-ups:
- Customer-facing statement draft (CS/PR review): link in 'links' below.
- Internal postmortem to be filed in Confluence (owner: Priya Sharma) and shared with product, solutions, and SRE.

Why this differs from prior rollouts:
Instead of a single catastrophic failure we observed a subtle, low-signal semantic drift that accumulated as traffic increased. This exposed a blind spot in both shadow fidelity and health check design. The mitigations focus on improving the observability and reproducibility of stateful behaviors (KV cache, long prefixes) and adding explicit quality gates to rollouts.

acceptance_criteria: Synthetic safety-suite runs as part of pre-release CI and fails the pipeline on quality regression
Shadow path reproduces KV cache behavior for >95% of production traces during smoke tests
Automated rollback triggers on synthetic-run quality failure within configured SLA (3 minutes)
Runbook published in Console and linked from rollout UI; on-call rotation trained on steps
tests: Synthetic corpus: 10k inputs covering multi-turn state, long prefixes (>1k tokens), and structured schema prompts
Shadow fidelity test: replay 1% of production trace with KV warmup enabled and compare cache hit patterns
Stress ramp test: simulate 1%->10%->50% ramp under background noise and validate divergence detector
Quantization stability test: run candidate vs baseline at 1k/2k/4k prefix lengths and compare output distributions
